text:
Rep: Wren, Emeka, thank you for sticking with this. I know it's been a long road.
Wren Dunmore (Operations Manager): It has, and I'll be honest, I'm worn out. Seventy people, two states, and for three weeks I've been trying to get a straight number in front of Emeka. Here's the number. Your quote works out to about fourteen dollars per employee per month. Call it eleven thousand, seven hundred sixty a year. And I've got a quote for about seven thousand from someone else.
Rep: That's a big gap. Can I ask what you're comparing?
Wren: Payroll and PTO. Basic stuff. I like that yours does more, I do. I told Emeka, the onboarding looks great. But I can't pay for things I'm not going to use this year.
Emeka Rourke (Finance Director): Let me be plain about it. The board approved eight thousand for this item. I could stretch to nine if I move something from facilities. Eleven seven is not possible. I'm not able to justify it, even if the product is better.
Wren: And it is better. That's the frustrating part.
Rep: Is there a package that might work?
Emeka: We'd have to see a number under nine. I'm not holding my breath.
Rep: I'll look at what we can do.
Wren: I appreciate it. But I'll tell you now, if I don't hear back by Friday, we'll sign with the cheaper one. We have to be live by January.
Emeka: Honestly, that's the situation.
Rep: Understood.

Rep: Annelise, Ingrid, good morning. I appreciate you both taking the time.
Annelise Lindgren (COO): Good morning. I will be frank, as I would want someone to be with me. We have fifty-two employees across three locations, and the proposal you sent comes to approximately thirteen dollars per employee per month. That is about eight thousand one hundred per year. The alternative we are considering is closer to five thousand.
Rep: Thank you for being open about it. Are they comparable in scope?
Annelise: For our purposes, yes. Payroll, scheduling, and time off. We are a small hospitality business. Margins are thin, and the season has been softer than we hoped.
Ingrid Vasquez (Operations Director): I will add that I prefer your product. The scheduling screens are cleaner, and your team was far more responsive. But my budget is fixed. I have forty-eight hundred allocated, and I cannot go beyond it without approval I will not receive.
Annelise: I want to be clear that this is not a reflection on the quality. It is a question of what we can afford.
Rep: Would a reduced package be of interest?
Annelise: Possibly, if it came in near five thousand. I do not see how that would work with your structure.
Rep: I will check.
Ingrid: We would be glad to hear back, but please do not expect a change.

Subject: Our decision

Dear team,

Thank you for the time and care you put into our review. We have decided to proceed with the lower-cost option. Your quote was roughly $8,100 a year for our 52 employees and the alternative is closer to $5,000, which is within our fixed budget.

We thought highly of your product and your people.

Sincerely,
Annelise Lindgren

Rep: Noor, Kofi, thanks for coming back to me. I know it's been a few weeks.
Noor Thorsen (Operations Manager): Yeah, it has, hasn't it? Fourteen days between the first call and the demo, I think, I looked it up, and then another week of us not getting back. That's partly my fault, I'm wearing three hats here, ops, HR, a little bit of the front desk. Anyway. I wanted to tell you, we're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Thank you for telling me. Would you share what led you there?
Noor: It's kind of boring, honestly. Our broker. We've had the same broker forever, since before I got here, and they handle our renewals, and they brought the whole bundle to us, with the benefits side and the payroll side together. I asked, what about the other one, and our broker just said, honestly, this is the one that works best with the carriers they know. And I thought, well, they know what they're doing, I don't.
Kofi Okonkwo (CFO): From my side, I'd say the bundle was priced fine. Close to yours. It wasn't a money decision. It was the broker's recommendation and we want one person to call at renewal time.
Noor: Right, right. And your demo was nice, I liked it, the interface is lovely. I told Kofi, if it were up to me alone, I might've picked you. But I trust our broker, and fifty-four employees in two states, we don't need to complicate things.
Rep: I understand. Would you mind if I checked in next year?
Noor: Please do. I'd love that.

Rep: Omar, Maren, good to see you.
Omar Dunmore (VP of People): Hey. I'll get to it. It's the money. Seventy-two employees, one state. Your yearly quote is about twelve thousand. I've got Tallyhold at roughly seven thousand five hundred. That's a four-and-a-half-thousand gap, and I can't explain it away.
Rep: Is the scope the same?
Omar: Close. Payroll, time off, a bit of reporting. Yours has more bells, I'll give you that. We don't use them.
Maren Whitlock (Finance Director): I'll be blunt. We're a small shop and we had a rough second quarter. My ceiling for this was eight thousand. I told Omar, even if I loved your product, I can't get to twelve.
Omar: And she's not wrong. I'd have been fine paying ten, maybe. Twelve, no.
Rep: Would a smaller package change the picture?
Omar: If it came in near eight, sure. But you said the floor was around ten.
Rep: That's right.
Omar: Then we're done, I think. It was a good demo. The person you sent was patient with me, I asked her dumb questions. I just can't make the number work.
Maren: We're tired of this too. We just need it over with.
Rep: I understand. Thanks for being straight with me.
Omar: Of course. If your pricing changes, call me.

Rep: Nadia, Yuki, thanks for taking the call. I got your note.
Nadia Moreau (COO): Yeah. Thanks for making time, I know you were hoping to move this week. It's not the answer you wanted. Honestly, we're stopping. We aren't picking anybody else. We're staying with what we have, for now.
Rep: Can you tell me what happened?
Nadia: Our owner pulled the plug on a handful of projects. We lost the biggest outdoor retail contract in September, and everything that wasn't keeping the lights on went in a drawer. Payroll migration was on the list. We have eighty-eight people, one state, and I'd honestly been looking forward to it, but it's a budget freeze, plain and simple.
Yuki Brannigan (Compliance Lead): And my project, the compliance audit, got put off too. I was going to use your system for it. So it's not that you did something wrong. If anything, I wanted it.
Nadia: Yes. I don't want you thinking it was the demo or the quote. Both were fine. It's just not the year for it.
Rep: I appreciate that. Is there a point when it might come back?
Nadia: I'd guess spring. Maybe summer. Our owner said to revisit after the first of next year. I'm tired, honestly. I wish I had better news.
Yuki: We'll reach out.

Subject: On hold for now

Hi,

A quick note to say we are pausing the payroll project. Our owner froze new spending after a lost contract, so we are not moving forward with anyone. It had nothing to do with your demo or your quote. We hope to revisit in the spring.

Thanks for your patience,
Nadia

Rep: Ingrid, Hollis, good morning.
Ingrid Ivarsson (Director of Operations): Morning. I'll keep this brisk. We've decided on Tallyhold.
Rep: Thanks for telling me. What led you there?
Ingrid: Our broker. They handle our renewals, and they brought us the package, payroll and benefits together. Our broker said it's the best fit for a company our size. Fifty-two people, three states. We trust them. They've been with us for years.
Hollis Nakamura (HR Director): I'll add, I liked your demo. Said so. But the broker put that bundle in front of us, and it came with the benefits feeds already set up. That saves me a lot of work in November, when enrollment is open.
Ingrid: Right. It's one invoice, one contact. Our broker is the person I'd call anyway.
Rep: Was there anything in our product that fell short?
Ingrid: No. Honestly, no. It wasn't product. It was the broker's recommendation.
Hollis: And the broker takes care of the renewals. I don't want to be in the middle if something goes sideways.
Rep: That makes sense. May I check in next year?
Ingrid: Sure. If the situation changes, we'll tell you.
Hollis: Thanks for the effort. It was a good process.
Ingrid: Yes. Thank you.

Rep: Marisol, Maren, good afternoon.
Marisol Eastwood (Office Manager): Afternoon. I will be direct. It comes down to cost. We have seventy-nine employees in one state. Your quote is thirteen dollars per employee per month, so about twelve thousand, three hundred a year. Tallyhold's proposal is about eight thousand five hundred. The difference is roughly thirty-eight hundred dollars.
Rep: Is the scope equivalent?
Marisol: Nearly. Payroll, time off, and basic reporting. We don't use your performance module, or the onboarding workflows. So the extra capability has no value to us this year.
Maren Eastwood (Finance Director): My budget line for this is nine thousand. I can't exceed it. I looked at the numbers twice. If your quote had been near ten, I would have taken it to the owner. At twelve three, I can't.
Marisol: One more point, for the record. It took fourteen days to get from the first call to the demo. That's not why we're leaving. It's a minor thing, and I understand calendars. But I did note it.
Maren: Agreed. It was minor.
Rep: Thank you. Is there a package structure that might help?
Marisol: If you could reach nine, I'd listen. I don't expect that.
Rep: I'll check what I can do.
Maren: Please send anything by Friday. We're finalizing next week.

Rep: Casper, thanks for picking up. I know it's been about a week since the demo, so I wanted to check in before the quarter closes out.
Casper Okonkwo (Office Manager): Yes, hi, good to hear from you. Let me be organized about this, because I did write it down. We had the intro call, then the demo on, what was it, day seven, and the whole thing ran about fifty minutes. Sunniva joined for the second half.
Rep: She did, and she asked some sharp questions about the three-state setup.
Sunniva Santangelo (Operations Director): I did, and I thought your answers were clear. Eighty-nine people across three states is not nothing, and nobody got defensive. I appreciated that.
Casper Okonkwo (Office Manager): Right. So the headline is, we've decided to go a different direction. We're making a change, but it's not the one we first scoped with you.
Rep: Understood. Would it be useful if I walked through anything again, or is it settled?
Casper Okonkwo (Office Manager): It's settled, really. I'd say settled about, what, ten days ago, but I wanted to tell you properly rather than just go quiet. Honestly everyone on your side was lovely. Twelve emails back and forth and every one answered the same day, I counted.
Sunniva Santangelo (Operations Director): Thirteen, I think. Anyway, it was a pleasure.
Rep: That's kind. If anything shifts down the road, you know where we are. Can I ask anything about the direction, just so I can learn from it?
Casper Okonkwo (Office Manager): Ha, no, I think we'll leave it there. It's the direction we're going and we feel good about it. We just wanted you to hear it from us.
Rep: Fair enough. Is it all right if I check in again in about a year?
Casper Okonkwo (Office Manager): Please do. Put it on a calendar somewhere. Maybe a year, maybe eighteen months. And thank you again for the time, and for the follow-up notes. Those were tidy.
Sunniva Santangelo (Operations Director): Agreed. Best of luck with the rest of the year.
Rep: You too. Take care, both of you.

Rep: Omar, Linnea, thanks for making time. Last time you said you wanted to see numbers before the end of the week.
Omar Parekh (HR Director): Yes. I'll be direct, because I've already run this against our budget. You quoted us roughly nineteen thousand a year for eighty-one employees. That works out to about two hundred thirty-five per head. Our approved line for this whole category is closer to fourteen.
Rep: Okay. Is that a ceiling, or is there flexibility?
Omar Parekh (HR Director): It's a ceiling. Finance signed off on fourteen in January and I'm not getting a revision before next fiscal year.
Linnea Fonseca (Payroll Manager): And the other option, Brasswick, came in at about one seventy a head. So roughly thirteen-eight total. Which fits.
Rep: And on the product side, were there gaps that worried you?
Omar Parekh (HR Director): Not really. The demo was fine. Actually the demo was better than fine, the time-off screens are nicer. It's just the number. If it were four thousand lower we wouldn't be having this conversation.
Linnea Fonseca (Payroll Manager): Or if we only had to cover one state. We have two, and the second one is what pushes the tier up.
Rep: I can ask whether we can restructure the tier, but I don't want to promise.
Omar Parekh (HR Director): Please don't promise. I'd rather you be honest. We'll go with the cheaper one, and I'll send a note so it's in writing.

Subject: Decision on payroll platform

Hi,

Thank you both for the time and for the straight answers. We've decided to go with Brasswick. At roughly $19,000 a year for 81 people, yours sits well above our approved budget of about $14,000, and theirs came in under it. The product was good. Please keep us in mind if pricing changes.

Omar Parekh
HR Director, Elmcroft Outfitters

Rep: Nadia, I appreciate you taking the call. I wanted to hear how things are shaking out on your end.
Nadia Delacroix (COO): Oh, of course. Well, I'll just say it straight, we've decided to go a different direction. I mean, I was going to email, but I thought, no, a call is nicer. You folks were so patient. Sorry, I'm blabbing. I always do that when I feel a little bad.
Rep: No need to feel bad. Is there anything we could have done differently?
Nadia Delacroix (COO): Oh, gosh. No, no. Nothing like that. It's, you know, we're making a change, and that's the best way I can put it. It's a good change. For us.
Nadia Thorsen (Head of People): And I just want to add, the demo was lovely, and the team was very kind to both of us. Truly.
Nadia Delacroix (COO): Yes, what she said. Two Nadias, one thank-you.
Rep: Ha, I'll take it. Would it be okay if I stayed in touch?
Nadia Delacroix (COO): Please, yes. Send me a holiday card or something. Or one of those little newsletters, I do read them, I just don't answer them.
Nadia Thorsen (Head of People): I'll keep the notes you sent in our shared folder, in case.
Rep: That works for me. Thanks, both of you.
Nadia Delacroix (COO): Thank you. Truly. Okay, I'm going to let you go before I start telling you about my weekend.

Rep: Annelise, thanks. Marisol joining too?
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): Yes. She's here. Go ahead.
Rep: I wanted to hear where you are on the proposal.
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): Short version. It's too much. We have seventy-three people. Your number was about sixteen thousand a year. We budgeted ten.
Marisol Ashgrove (General Manager): Ten, max. I told Annelise ten.
Rep: Is that ten all in, including implementation?
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): Ten all in. First year.
Rep: And do you have another quote?
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): We do. Brasswick. About nine-two for the year. Setup is included. I checked.
Marisol Ashgrove (General Manager): It's not that I don't like your product. I do. The demo was good. But I run a print shop. I can't explain a six thousand dollar difference to the owner.
Rep: I understand. I could look at whether there's a smaller package.
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): Would it get to ten?
Rep: I'm not sure it would.
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): Then there's no point. We'd rather just go. No hard feelings.
Marisol Ashgrove (General Manager): None. Thank you for the time.
Rep: Thank you. If your budget moves, call me.
Annelise Underhill (HR Generalist): We will.

Rep: Thaddeus, Wren, thanks for jumping back on. Let's hear where you've landed.
Wren Lindgren (People Operations Lead): Okay, so I'll lay out the numbers, because I like numbers. Your annual quote for seventy-four people is around twenty-one thousand. The alternative we looked at is about fifteen-five. So we're talking a gap of five and a half thousand, roughly seventy-five dollars a head per year.
Thaddeus Dunmore (HR Director): Our hospitality margins are thin. Five and a half thousand is two part-time salaries for us over a quarter. I can't wave that away.
Rep: Understood. Is the cheaper option covering the same ground?
Wren Lindgren (People Operations Lead): Mostly. There's one thing, we wanted approvals with three or four steps, manager, then GM, then payroll. Yours does one or two. That's a nuisance, but we could live with it.
Thaddeus Dunmore (HR Director): We'd have worked around it. I mention it only for completeness.
Wren Lindgren (People Operations Lead): Totally minor. The honest answer is the price.
Rep: Anything else I should know?
Wren Lindgren (People Operations Lead): Well, since you ask, the mobile app. My front-desk lead tried the trial. She'd log in on her phone, get kicked out about every ten minutes, and then the clock-in screen froze on her twice during a shift change. She was livid. But that's not why. I told her it's a thing to fix, not a deal-breaker.
Thaddeus Dunmore (HR Director): Right, it's fixable. The money isn't, for us, this year.
Rep: I appreciate the candor. I'll pass the app notes to product.
Wren Lindgren (People Operations Lead): Please do. And thanks, the demo was clean.

Rep: Sunniva, Fenella, thanks for hopping on. Where do things stand?
Sunniva Fonseca (Head of HR): Frozen, honestly. Our CFO put a hold on all new spending last Tuesday. Not just us. Everything that isn't already contracted.
Rep: Ah. Is there a date it might lift?
Sunniva Fonseca (Head of HR): Nobody will say. Maybe after the board meets. So I can't sign anything and I can't even promise a timeline.
Fenella Ibarra (IT Manager): And just so you know, it's not about you. We liked the demo. Compliance liked it. We didn't talk to anybody else.
Rep: That's good to know. Is the freeze across the company?
Sunniva Fonseca (Head of HR): Company-wide. Mostly it's the priorities moving around. The thing everyone's chasing now is the product launch, and HR systems are in the maybe pile.
Fenella Ibarra (IT Manager): One tiny thing, since you asked last time for feedback. The mobile app. I tested it on my phone and it logged me out every time I switched to another app. And then the timesheet screen just hung. Not a big deal now, but when we revisit, that'd be on my list.
Rep: Noted, thanks. I'll flag it. Can I check back in early next quarter?
Sunniva Fonseca (Head of HR): Yes, please. Early January. If the freeze lifts, you're first call.
Rep: Great. Thanks, both.

Rep: Hollis, Signe, good to talk. Where did you end up?
Hollis Fonseca (VP of People): Short version, we're going with Tallyhold. It came down to dollars.
Rep: Can you share the numbers?
Hollis Fonseca (VP of People): Sure. You quoted us about twenty-six thousand a year for sixty-two people. Tallyhold is at nineteen-two. Call it a hundred and ten dollars less per head. That's roughly seven thousand a year.
Signe Thorsen (COO): And I'll be honest, we only budgeted twenty at the top. Anything above that I'd have to take to the owners, and I'm not going to do that over HR software.
Rep: Understood. Was there anything in the product that gave you pause?
Hollis Fonseca (VP of People): No. It's good. The reporting was fine, onboarding looked fine. One small thing, and I do mean small, it took thirteen days to get the demo on the calendar after our first call. I'd have liked sooner. But that didn't change anything. If your price had been under twenty, I'd have signed.
Signe Thorsen (COO): Yes. Nineteen-two plays in our budget, twenty-six doesn't.
Rep: Is there any room for a conversation if we revisit the tier?
Hollis Fonseca (VP of People): We've already told Tallyhold yes, so I don't want to reopen it. But thanks for the offer. I appreciate how clear your proposal was.
Rep: Thanks, both. If anything changes at renewal, reach out.
Signe Thorsen (COO): Will do.

Rep: Linnea, thanks for squeezing me in. Mirela's on as well?
Linnea Hollander (Director of Operations): She is. We have fifteen minutes, so I'll be quick.
Rep: Go ahead.
Linnea Hollander (Director of Operations): We're not going ahead. Money. Your proposal is just over twenty-two thousand for the year, sixty-four people, one state. That's about three-forty-five a head.
Mirela Santangelo (Head of Finance): Which, in my spreadsheet, is nearly six thousand more than Brasswick. Their quote is sixteen-four, and it includes the same payroll runs and the time-off module.
Rep: Is the Brasswick quote comparable on support and implementation?
Linnea Hollander (Director of Operations): Close enough. We'd lose a bit on hand-holding. But we're a food company with one state to file in, so we're not complicated.
Mirela Santangelo (Head of Finance): I can't justify six thousand extra for hand-holding.
Rep: Would it help if I looked at a reduced package for a single-state company?
Linnea Hollander (Director of Operations): You can look. I doubt you'll get near sixteen.
Rep: Probably not. I'll be honest about that.
Linnea Hollander (Director of Operations): Appreciated. We'd rather be clear than waste your time. Thanks for everything. The demo was good. It's just the budget.
Mirela Santangelo (Head of Finance): Agreed. Thank you.

Rep: Nadia, Annelise, thanks. I've got your note from yesterday. Walk me through it.
Nadia Brannigan (Operations Manager): Yeah. Okay. I'm tired, so I'll be plain. We need to hand our board a pack every quarter. Headcount by department, turnover, cost per hire, overtime trend. Different cut every time, because they keep changing what they want to see.
Annelise Whitlock (CFO): And your reporting is, what, fixed templates? We can export to a spreadsheet, fine, but I'm not rebuilding that pack by hand four times a year. Corvane lets us build the views ourselves. That's the thing.
Rep: We have some custom filters, but I understand that's not a full builder.
Nadia Brannigan (Operations Manager): Right. And I did ask three times in the demo, and the answer was always, it's on the roadmap.
Annelise Whitlock (CFO): Roadmap doesn't help me in March.
Rep: Fair. Was anything else a factor?
Annelise Whitlock (CFO): The price was higher too, a bit. But if the reporting worked, I'd have found the money. It's not the main point.
Nadia Brannigan (Operations Manager): The main point is the board pack. We've got fifty-eight people, it's not complicated except for that.
Rep: I appreciate you saying so.
Nadia Brannigan (Operations Manager): Sorry it's not better news.

Subject: Following up on our decision

Hi,

Thank you for the time you gave us over the last few weeks. We've decided to go with Corvane. The deciding factor was reporting: each quarter our board asks for a different cut of headcount, turnover and overtime, and we need to build those views ourselves instead of relying on fixed templates. Lanternmere's roadmap may get there, but we needed it now. Pricing was a smaller consideration, though Corvane was somewhat lower. The team was helpful throughout.

Best,
Nadia Brannigan
Operations Manager, Dunstan Media

Rep: Dariusz, Calla, thanks for hopping on. I was hoping for an update on the timeline.
Dariusz Fonseca (People Operations Lead): Yes. So, there's not much to say, and that's the update. Everything's paused.
Rep: Paused, okay. What happened?
Dariusz Fonseca (People Operations Lead): Our practice owner is reconsidering a bunch of stuff. They're looking at whether to merge two of the clinics. Until that's decided, nobody wants to move payroll. It'd be silly to migrate and then migrate again.
Calla Vasquez (HR Director): Agreed. And this is on me to say, it's not the demo and it's not the quote. Both were fine. If the merger doesn't happen, we'll probably pick this up again.
Rep: Do you have a sense of when you'll know?
Dariusz Fonseca (People Operations Lead): Spring, maybe. Realistically, I'd say after tax season.
Rep: Will you be speaking to anyone else in the meantime?
Calla Vasquez (HR Director): No. We haven't spoken to anyone else, we're not going to until this clears. Ninety-eight employees, one state, it's not that we need to rush.
Rep: Understood. Would it help if I kept the quote available?
Dariusz Fonseca (People Operations Lead): Yes, if you can hold the numbers. Don't promise the price but, you know, keep it handy.
Rep: I'll check back in April.
Dariusz Fonseca (People Operations Lead): Perfect. Thanks for being patient.

Rep: Ingrid, hi, how's your week going?
Ingrid Underhill (Director of Operations): Oh, busy, you know how it is in a dental group, somebody's always out, somebody's chair is double-booked. But good, good. I wanted to talk to you before Jules does, because he'll be blunter than me.
Jules Fairweather (Finance Director): I heard that.
Ingrid Underhill (Director of Operations): It's true, though. Okay, so. We loved the demo. The onboarding stuff, great. The thing is, your price for seventy-five people comes to about twenty thousand, and we found something for around fourteen. That's, what, eighty dollars a head different?
Jules Fairweather (Finance Director): Eighty-ish, yes. Six thousand over the year. For a group our size, in one state, I can't make the case for the more expensive one. We're not that complicated.
Rep: Is the cheaper one comparable on payroll accuracy?
Ingrid Underhill (Director of Operations): It seems fine. I mean we haven't lived with it. Oh, and also, honestly, the owner was talking about putting the whole thing on hold anyway, for a while, because of the new office buildout. So the timing wasn't great regardless. But that's more of a side thing. The money is really the thing.
Jules Fairweather (Finance Director): The buildout's eating budget, yes. But if your price had been in the fourteen range we'd have pushed through.
Rep: Understood. Thank you for being open about it.
Ingrid Underhill (Director of Operations): Of course! You were so patient with us. We'll stay in touch.

Rep: Teodoro, thanks for taking the call. I know it's been a while.
Teodoro Dunmore (Office Manager): Eleven days. I looked it up. Eleven days between our first conversation and the demo.
Rep: I'm sorry about that. Our calendar was tight.
Teodoro Dunmore (Office Manager): I understand. But by day eleven, the sponsor, our partner who was pushing this, had lost steam. She told me, find something, anything, so we can stop doing payroll in spreadsheets. So I did. I started a trial of something else on day eight, and by the time your demo happened we were already loading employee records into it.
Thaddeus Thorsen (Payroll Manager): Eighty-eight people, and I'd already done two practice payruns on the other one. I can't throw that away.
Rep: Did the demo show anything you disliked?
Teodoro Dunmore (Office Manager): No. It looked good. Honestly, if it had been day three, I think we'd be signing with you. Day eleven was too late.
Rep: That's fair feedback, and I'll pass it on.
Thaddeus Thorsen (Payroll Manager): Thanks for the courtesy, though.

Subject: Our decision

Hi,

Thank you for walking us through Lanternmere HR. I wanted to put in writing what I said on the phone. Eleven days passed between our first call and the demo, and in that time our partner had run out of patience and I had already started setting up another system, with employee records loaded and practice payruns done. By the time we saw yours, switching would have meant starting over. The demo itself looked good. A faster turnaround might have changed things.

Teodoro Dunmore
Office Manager, Umber Design Studio

Rep: Kwame, Noor, thanks. Let's talk about where you are.
Kwame Galbraith (Head of HR): Short answer. We're going with Tallyhold.
Rep: Okay. May I ask what tipped it?
Kwame Galbraith (Head of HR): Our broker. He's the one who handles our renewals, medical, dental, all of it. He put Tallyhold in front of us as a bundle. Payroll plus benefits admin. One invoice.
Noor Yarrow (Finance Director): We've worked with him eleven years. He's never steered us wrong. I asked him point blank, is Lanternmere a problem? He said no, they're fine, but this is easier for you.
Rep: Did the bundle price compare to ours?
Kwame Galbraith (Head of HR): Didn't dig in. It's the bundle he put in front of us. I trust him.
Noor Yarrow (Finance Director): Yes. It's more about who's calling us in November when the renewal hits. He is.
Rep: I understand. Anything in the demo that was a concern?
Kwame Galbraith (Head of HR): No. Demo was good. Eighty people, three states, yours handled it. But the broker thing is the decision.
Rep: Thank you for being straightforward.
Kwame Galbraith (Head of HR): Sure. Send me the follow-up if there is one.

Subject: Thanks, and our decision

Hi,

Thanks to you and the team for the time. We've decided to go with Tallyhold. Our benefits broker, who handles our renewals every year, recommended their bundle of payroll and benefits administration, and we're following his advice. We've worked with him a long time and trust his judgment. This isn't a reflection on Lanternmere HR; the demo was solid and your team was easy to work with. If our situation changes, I'll reach out.

Kwame Galbraith
Head of HR, Elmcroft Robotics

Rep: Annelise, Delphine, thanks for the call. Where are we?
Annelise Ivarsson (HR Generalist): Not far. We're stuck. Leadership froze the project.
Rep: Do you know why?
Annelise Ivarsson (HR Generalist): The VP who wanted it moved to another division. Nobody inherited it. So it sits.
